tells.1: Four identical “Mitigation:” tags and mirror-image sections read like a filled-in template, not someone making a case.
tells.2: Even four-part balance and leftover stock lines (“pulled into renewal terms by default,” “spread management attention and cash thin”) still sound generated.
tells.4: Every bullet gets the same bold mini-headline, and “I’m glad to walk through” is an unnatural swap for “happy to.”
tells.5: One-word bold labels such as “Flexibility.” plus repeated “Mitigation:” prefixes are classic generated-list formatting.
tells.6: Markdown ## headers and flat, person-free sentences; “declining structurally” is a stiff reorder of the same template line.

reason: Version 3 is the only draft with a hasty, idiosyncratic voice; the rest share one template, with 2 and 4 the least mechanical. I would send 4 because it stays clear and credible, with a spoken cadence, and avoids both version 2’s muddled “good reasons” line and the canned Mitigation labels.
